name: Península Valdés
blurb: Right whales, orcas on the beach, elephant seals and penguins.

tip.title: Remove the orcas
tip.text: Orcas take sea lions and elephant seals from the beach. Set Orca to -100% and watch sea lions, seals and the animals they eat.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light powers the plankton of the gulfs and the sparse shrubs of the steppe.

nodes.name: Cold, nutrient-rich gulf waters
nodes.desc: The sheltered gulfs of the peninsula hold the plankton and fish that the whales, seals and penguins depend on.

nodes.name: Dry westerly wind & low rain
nodes.desc: The peninsula is a cold desert with roughly 240 mm of rain a year and winds mainly from the west, which keeps the vegetation low and shrubby.

nodes.name: Sandy, salty steppe soil
nodes.desc: Thin, dry ground broken by salt lakes supports mostly low shrubs.

nodes.name: Bacteria, fungi & beetles
nodes.desc: Break down carcasses, dung and dead plants and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae that float in the gulfs and open sea and feed krill and small fish, forming the base of the marine web.

nodes.name: Chuquiraga shrubs
nodes.desc: Spiny evergreen shrubs of dry Patagonian steppe. GBIF records several species around the peninsula.

nodes.name: Lycium (matorral shrubs)
nodes.desc: Thorny desert shrubs recorded on the peninsula. Maras are reported to eat Lycium among other shrubs and herbs.

nodes.name: Saltbush
nodes.desc: A salt-tolerant shrub of dry ground that suits the salty soils. Maras are reported to eat it.

nodes.name: Antarctic krill
nodes.desc: Small shrimp-like crustaceans that filter phytoplankton and are eaten by whales, seals, penguins and seabirds. They live mainly in the Southern Ocean, where right whales are thought to feed.

nodes.name: Argentine anchoita
nodes.desc: A small schooling fish of the Argentine coast that feeds on zooplankton and is prey for larger fish, squid, sea lions and penguins.

nodes.name: Guanaco
nodes.desc: A grazer and browser of grasses, shrubs and herbs that lives across Patagonia. Pumas and foxes are its natural predators elsewhere.

nodes.name: Patagonian mara
nodes.desc: A large cavy that eats mostly grasses and shrubs such as Atriplex lampa and Lycium. Foxes and birds of prey hunt the young.

nodes.name: Southern right whale
nodes.desc: Breeds in the gulfs from May to December and feeds on zooplankton, mainly krill. Calves are pecked by kelp gulls, and orcas are its only known predator.

nodes.name: Magellanic penguin
nodes.desc: Eats small fish such as anchoita, plus squid and krill. Wikipedia reports about 150,000 breeding pairs at the peninsula.

nodes.name: Southern elephant seal
nodes.desc: Dives deep for squid and fish and also eats krill. Valdés is the only continental breeding colony, and orcas take weaned pups and juveniles.

nodes.name: South American sea lion
nodes.desc: Eats fish such as anchovies and hake, squid and sometimes penguins. At Valdés orcas beach themselves to grab it near shore.

nodes.name: Kelp gull
nodes.desc: An omnivorous gull that scavenges and hunts. Since at least 1996 it has pecked at living right whales off Valdés.

nodes.name: Southern giant petrel
nodes.desc: Eats fish, krill, squid and carrion, including carcasses of elephant seals. GloBI records it eating right whale and Magellanic penguin.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A carrion-eating bird. GloBI holds records of it eating Magellanic penguins.

nodes.name: Pampas fox
nodes.desc: An omnivorous canid that eats birds, rodents, hares, fruit and carrion. Hunts young maras.

nodes.name: Orca
nodes.desc: Valdés orcas hunt sea lions and elephant seals in shallow water, sometimes beaching briefly to grab prey. The behaviour is learned and practised over years.
